A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JointAVBench and provide readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices A–H. Corresponding material can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, modality ablations, human annotation analyses, and audio-visual correlation measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations, reports recomputed model results using audited labels, and includes benchmark-quality measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and new Appendix A.4 add a post-verification answer-label audit combining an external LLM auditor with human annotations through majority voting, retaining the original label when no majority exists. This extends the otherwise retained benchmark-construction pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the SF20K-derived benchmark with 2,853 questions, 15 tasks, four audio types, and three scene spans. The additional audit explicitly changes labels without removing samples. The datasets evaluated for audio-visual correlation also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 evaluates the same 17 models in both versions. Table 4 retains the same four models and their audio-only, video-only, and combined-input comparisons. Changed rankings and row order do not introduce new comparators.

E3.justification: The reference answers underlying the entire model evaluation are revised: v2 explicitly recomputes all reported experimental results using audited labels instead of the original human-verified labels (Appendices A.4 and A.6). This substantially changes the basis for scoring correctness, although the retained frame-sampling, model configurations, and accuracy metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes the reported 400-sample annotation-reliability analysis. It also revises the evidence in the existing modality ablation, including VideoLLaMA2's equal counts of fusion wins and losses. The task breakdowns, scene-count analysis, and Appendix C.2 failure cases remain; no new robustness investigation is added.

E5.justification: v1 reports independent annotation by two annotators on 400 randomly selected samples and Cohen's kappa of 0.713; v2 removes this quantitative inter-annotator validation entirely. Section 4.1 adds a deterministic-inference stability assertion, but supplies no run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or replacement agreement statistic.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 and Figures 4–7 substantially revise results. Gemini2.5-Pro changes from 62.6% to 65.3%; Gemini2.5-Flash changes from 52.6% to 58.0% and overtakes Qwen2.5-Omni. These are recomputed results under audited labels, not demonstrated same-setting model improvements. Tables 1 and 6 change automatic AV-correlation scores from 100% to 80.4% for OmniBench, 99.0% for AV-Odyssey, and 93.5% for JointAVBench; human scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical results or proofs. v2 clarifies that N_o counts performance above the best single-modality score and N_u counts performance below the worst; these rules already reproduce v1's Table 4 counts, so this is explanatory clarification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark scope, construction contribution, and central claim that current models have substantial joint audio-visual reasoning limitations. Updating the reported accuracy ceiling changes supporting results rather than the scope of these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 qualifies fusion benefits from all models to most models and softens Qwen2.5-Omni's comparative interpretation. Appendix D adds specific limitations concerning caption/filtering errors, ambiguous options, residual weak modality dependency, and unverifiable overlap with proprietary training data.

D1.justification: v2 documents the audit's inputs, exclusion of evaluated-model outputs, voting, and fallback rule, although the auditor identity and voting configuration remain unspecified. Figure 13 corrects the modality-check prompt's otherwise verdict from YES to NO, and the project-page address changes. Existing hardware and decoding details are retained.

R1.justification: The Landis and Koch (1977) citation and reference disappear with the annotation-agreement analysis. The remaining cited works and the substantive related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds an audit subsection and acknowledgments, updates affiliations and publication headers, and makes localized explanatory and grammatical edits. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4–7 are redrawn with revised results and some changed axis ranges; Figures 4–5 move onto the page containing Figures 6–7, and Table 4 moves to the following page. Table rows are reordered, but the same seven tables and sixteen figures remain with largely unchanged display structures.

improvement.justification: Correcting the modality-check prompt, qualifying fusion interpretations, and expanding limitations improve clarity. However, v2 removes v1's 400-sample agreement evidence and bases revised results on an insufficiently specified label audit, without reporting its correction count or demonstrating improved label accuracy. These benefits and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
